audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for vineyard tenants, cornerstone, Caesar/image, resurrection dispute, greatest command, David/Lord question, scribes warning, and widow offering.

verses.restored: He began to speak to them in parables: A person planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, built a tower, leased it to farmers, and went away.

familiar.text: And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.

modern.text: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

original.text: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς ⸀λαλεῖν· Ἀμπελῶνα ⸂ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν⸃, καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.

verses.restored: At the season he sent a servant to the farmers so that he might receive from the farmers some of the fruit of the vineyard.

familiar.text: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.

modern.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον, ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ ⸂τῶν καρπῶν⸃ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος·

verses.restored: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.

familiar.text: And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.

modern.text: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

original.text: ⸀καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν.

verses.restored: Again he sent to them another servant; that one they struck on the head and dishonored.

familiar.text: And again he sent unto them another servant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.

modern.text: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.

original.text: καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον· ⸀κἀκεῖνον ⸀ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ⸀ἠτίμασαν.

verses.restored: He sent another, and that one they killed; and many others, some they beat and some they killed.

familiar.text: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.

modern.text: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν· κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν, καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους, ⸂οὓς μὲν δέροντες οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες⸃.

verses.restored: He still had one, a beloved son. Last he sent him to them, saying, They will respect my son.

familiar.text: Having yet therefore one son, his wellbeloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.

modern.text: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

original.text: ἔτι ⸂ἕνα εἶχεν, υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἀπέστειλεν⸃ αὐτὸν ⸂ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς⸃ λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.

verses.restored: But those farmers said to themselves, This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.

familiar.text: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be our’s.

modern.text: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

original.text: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ ⸂πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν⸃ ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία.

verses.restored: Taking him, they killed him and threw him outside the vineyard.

familiar.text: And they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.

modern.text: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

original.text: καὶ λαβόντες ⸂ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν⸃ ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος.

verses.restored: What will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.

familiar.text: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.

modern.text: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.

original.text: ⸀τί ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος; ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις.

verses.restored: Have you not read this Scripture: The stone the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner;

familiar.text: And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner:

modern.text: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

original.text: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας·

verses.restored: from the Lord this came to be, and it is marvelous in our eyes?

familiar.text: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?

modern.text: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’ ?”

original.text: παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;

verses.restored: They were seeking to seize him, yet feared the crowd, for they knew he spoke the parable against them. Leaving him, they went away.

familiar.text: And they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people: for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way.

modern.text: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away. Paying Taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:15–22; Luke 20:19–26)

original.text: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν. καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον.

verses.restored: They send to him some of the Pharisees and Herodians, so that they might catch him in word.

familiar.text: And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.

modern.text: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.

original.text: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ.

verses.restored: Coming, they said to him, Teacher, we know you are true and do not care about anyone's status, for you do not look at people's face, but teach the way of the Divine in truth. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not? Should we give, or should we not give?

familiar.text: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

modern.text: “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one. Indeed, You are impartial and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay them or not?”

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλʼ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις· ἔξεστιν ⸂δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι⸃ ἢ οὔ; δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν;

verses.restored: Knowing their hypocrisy, he said to them, Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius so I may see it.

familiar.text: Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why tempt ye me? bring me a penny, that I may see it.

modern.text: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὴν ὑπόκρισιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί με πειράζετε; φέρετέ μοι δηνάριον ἵνα ἴδω.

verses.restored: They brought one. He said to them, Whose image and inscription is this? They said to him, Caesar's.

familiar.text: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Caesar’s.

modern.text: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν. καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Give back the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of the Divine to the Divine. And they marveled at him.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. And they marvelled at him.

modern.text: Then Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And they marveled at Him. The Sadducees and the Resurrection (Matthew 22:23–33; Luke 20:27–40)

original.text: ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· ⸂Τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε⸃ Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ. καὶ ⸀ἐξεθαύμαζον ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Sadducees came to him, those saying there is no resurrection, and they questioned him, saying,

familiar.text: Then come unto him the Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,

modern.text: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him:

original.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται Σαδδουκαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν, οἵτινες λέγουσιν ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, καὶ ⸀ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες·

verses.restored: Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother should take the wife and raise up seed for his brother.

familiar.text: Master, Moses wrote unto us, If a man’s brother die, and leave his wife behind him, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

modern.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

original.text: Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ ⸂μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον⸃, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν ⸀γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying, left no seed.

familiar.text: Now there were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed.

modern.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.

original.text: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα·

verses.restored: The second took her and died, leaving no seed; and the third likewise.

familiar.text: And the second took her, and died, neither left he any seed: and the third likewise.

modern.text: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.

original.text: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἀπέθανεν ⸂μὴ καταλιπὼν⸃ σπέρμα, καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως·

verses.restored: The seven left no seed. Last of all, the woman also died.

familiar.text: And the seven had her, and left no seed: last of all the woman died also.

modern.text: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.

original.text: καὶ ⸂οἱ ἑπτὰ⸃ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα· ⸀ἔσχατον πάντων ⸂καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν⸃.

verses.restored: In the resurrection, when they rise, of which of them will she be wife? For the seven had her as wife.

familiar.text: In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her to wife.

modern.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”

original.text: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ⸂ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν⸃ τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Is this not why you wander: because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of the Divine?

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto them, Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?

modern.text: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?

original.text: ⸂ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ;

verses.restored: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like messengers in the heavens.

familiar.text: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven.

modern.text: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

original.text: ὅταν γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῶσιν, οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ⸀γαμίζονται, ἀλλʼ εἰσὶν ὡς ⸀ἄγγελοι ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·

verses.restored: Concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the bush passage, how the Divine spoke to him, saying, I am the Divine of Abraham, the Divine of Isaac, and the Divine of Jacob?

familiar.text: And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?

modern.text: But concerning the dead rising, have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses, how God told him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ?

original.text: περὶ δὲ τῶν νεκρῶν ὅτι ἐγείρονται οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ Μωϋσέως ἐπὶ τοῦ βάτου ⸀πῶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς λέγων· Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ⸂ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ⸃ θεὸς Ἰακώβ;

verses.restored: He is not Divine of dead ones, but of living ones. You wander greatly.

familiar.text: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.

modern.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!” The Greatest Commandment (Deuteronomy 6:1–19; Matthew 22:34–40)

original.text: οὐκ ἔστιν ⸀θεὸς νεκρῶν ⸀ἀλλὰ ζώντων· ⸀πολὺ πλανᾶσθε.

verses.restored: One of the scribes came, hearing them disputing, and seeing that he answered them beautifully, asked him, Which command is first of all?

familiar.text: And one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, Which is the first commandment of all?

modern.text: Now one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate. Noticing how well Jesus had answered them, he asked Him, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”

original.text: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συζητούντων, ⸀ἰδὼν ὅτι καλῶς ⸂ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς⸃, ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν· Ποία ἐστὶν ⸂ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων⸃;

verses.restored: Jesus answered, First is: Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord:

modern.text: Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.

original.text: ⸂ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ ὅτι Πρώτη ⸀ἐστίν· Ἄκουε, Ἰσραήλ, κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν,

verses.restored: You shall love the Lord your God from all your heart, from all your soul/life, from all your mind, and from all your strength.

familiar.text: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.

modern.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’

original.text: καὶ ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης ⸀τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος ⸀σου.

verses.restored: Second is this: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. No other command is greater than these.

familiar.text: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.

modern.text: The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandment is greater than these.”

original.text: ⸀δευτέρα αὕτη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν. μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν.

verses.restored: The scribe said to him, Beautifully said, Teacher; according to truth you said that he is one, and there is no other besides him.

familiar.text: And the scribe said unto him, Well, Master, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God; and there is none other but he:

modern.text: “Right, Teacher,” the scribe replied. “You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him,

original.text: ⸀καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ γραμματεύς· Καλῶς, διδάσκαλε, ἐπʼ ἀληθείας εἶπες ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος πλὴν αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: And to love him from the whole heart, whole understanding, and whole strength, and to love the neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

familiar.text: And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

modern.text: and to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, which is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

original.text: καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐξ ὅλης ⸀τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ⸀συνέσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν ⸀περισσότερόν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων καὶ θυσιῶν.

verses.restored: Jesus, seeing that he answered thoughtfully, said to him, You are not far from the reign of the Divine. And no one dared to question him anymore.

familiar.text: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.

modern.text: When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question Him any further. Whose Son Is the Christ? (Matthew 22:41–46; Luke 20:41–44)

original.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν ⸀αὐτὸν ὅτι νουνεχῶς ἀπεκρίθη εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐ μακρὰν εἶ ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι ἐτόλμα αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.

verses.restored: Answering as he taught in the temple, Jesus said, How do the scribes say that the Messiah is son of David?

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said, while he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that Christ is the son of David?

modern.text: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, He asked, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?

original.text: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· Πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς υἱὸς ⸂Δαυίδ ἐστιν⸃;

verses.restored: David himself said in the holy Spirit: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.

familiar.text: For David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The LORD said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool.

modern.text: Speaking by the Holy Spirit, David himself declared: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

original.text: ⸀αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ εἶπεν ἐν ⸂τῷ πνεύματι τῷ⸃ ἁγίῳ· ⸀Εἶπεν ⸀κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· ⸀Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ⸀ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου.

verses.restored: David himself calls him Lord; so how is he his son? The great crowd heard him gladly.

familiar.text: David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son? And the common people heard him gladly.

modern.text: David himself calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?” And the large crowd listened to Him with delight. Beware of the Scribes (Luke 20:45–47)

original.text: ⸀αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν κύριον, καὶ πόθεν ⸂αὐτοῦ ἐστιν υἱός⸃; καὶ ὁ πολὺς ὄχλος ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως.

verses.restored: In his teaching he said, Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk around in long robes, greetings in the marketplaces,

familiar.text: And he said unto them in his doctrine, Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces,

modern.text: In His teaching Jesus also said, “Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces,

original.text: Καὶ ⸂ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν⸃· Βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων ἐν στολαῖς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς

verses.restored: first seats in the synagogues and first places at feasts,

familiar.text: And the chief seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts:

modern.text: and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.

original.text: καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις,

verses.restored: who devour widows' houses and for appearance make long prayers. These will receive greater judgment.

familiar.text: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: these shall receive greater damnation.

modern.text: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.” The Widow’s Offering (Luke 21:1–4)

original.text: οἱ κατεσθίοντες τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι· οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα.

verses.restored: Sitting opposite the treasury, he watched how the crowd cast copper into the treasury. Many rich people cast in much.

familiar.text: And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.

modern.text: As Jesus was sitting opposite the treasury, He watched the crowd putting money into it. And many rich people put in large amounts.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀καθίσας ⸀κατέναντι τοῦ γαζοφυλακίου ἐθεώρει πῶς ὁ ὄχλος βάλλει χαλκὸν εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον· καὶ πολλοὶ πλούσιοι ἔβαλλον πολλά·

verses.restored: One poor widow came and cast in two small coins, which are a quadrans.

familiar.text: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.

modern.text: Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius.

original.text: καὶ ἐλθοῦσα μία χήρα πτωχὴ ἔβαλεν λεπτὰ δύο, ὅ ἐστιν κοδράντης.

verses.restored: Calling his disciples, he said to them, Amen, I say to you: this poor widow cast in more than all those casting into the treasury.

familiar.text: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:

modern.text: Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.

original.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ⸀εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ⸀ἔβαλεν τῶν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον·

verses.restored: For all cast in out of their abundance; but she, out of her lack, cast in all she had, her whole life/living.

familiar.text: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

modern.text: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”

original.text: πάντες γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τῆς ὑστερήσεως αὐτῆς πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν ἔβαλεν, ὅλον τὸν βίον αὐτῆς.
